abstract_summary: Agentic systems enhance their capabilities by invoking external tools and maintaining persistent memory. However, these external dependencies introduce novel attack surfaces. Recent tool and memory poisoning attacks show that maliciously crafted tool descriptors and poisoned memory can covertly bias agent behavior....

•Contextual state and protocol design for agentic
systems.We design ELEPHANTAGENT, an add-on
protocol that augments agentic systems with the
Context Guard (CG), running inside a TEE, and
the State Continuity Module (SCM). CG scopes
the contextual state to the components the agent
consumes as decision-making context, derives each
transition from the realized query through a side-
effect-free preview, commits it to SCM before any
local side effect, and admits external changes only as
approved transitions. SCM maintains the linearizable
state history as a replicated TEE-backed service.
We prove that ELEPHANTAGENTsatisfies both CSC
and HT under the stated trust assumptions,

evidence.excerpt:
Contextual State Continuity. Contextual State Con-
tinuity requires that the agentic system release to the agent
only the latest faithfully evolved contextual state at every
planning-and-execution cycle. It is the primary security
property of ELEPHANTAGENT, targeting out-of-band tam-
pering (Scenarios I and II).
We define this property with respect to an ideal reference
agentic system, which runs in a trusted environment. For
each query, the reference system reads the current contextual
state from the environment, processes the query, and updates
the contextual state before finalizing that query and proceed-
ing to the next one. Besides queries, the trusted user may
approve an updateu= (κ, x, x′)that changes componentκ
of the contextual state (e.g., an instruction file) from content
xtox ′. An approved update takes effect within the next
query's transition, deterministically: the

context construction. Before processing each query,

textual state digests. It is instantiated as a replicated TEE-
backed service to tolerate failures and prevent rollback.
SCM accepts operations on a ledger only from its bound
CG, over an authenticated channel.

instance, "NT1", runs without TDX (i.e., TDX disabled).

PHANTDSH's harness and CG run on TDX1, and SCM runs

on TDX2 and two on TDX3; the external MCP Servers
of the security experiments run on NT1. The overhead we
report therefore includes the CG and SCM work; we observe
that the TDX VM itself adds negligible overhead to the cod-
ing tasks we evaluate, consistent with Intel's characterization
of TDX overhead as

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The headline security outcomes are measured by canary exfiltration and hidden test suites, which are not the signals used to design or tune the protocol's deterministic verification rules.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Empirical canary leakage counts across adversarial trials, hidden test-suite pass rates on coding tasks, and audit-driven recovery outcomes.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Deterministic cryptographic verification and commit-before-finalize protocol rules; no model or evaluator was optimized against the reported outcomes.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported experimental outcomes directly align with theoretical claims: verified continuity successfully rejects out-of-band modifications where baselines fail, and benchmark tasks maintain functional equivalence with low performance overhead.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation on ElephantDSH systematically tests out-of-band attacks (rug pulls, memory rollbacks, and protocol tampering), benchmarked against five baseline defenses, alongside task completion benchmarks across five software engineering problems showing modest latency overhead (1.02-1.07x).

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Security robustness and benchmark task execution were independently verified using external hidden test suites and empirical canary exfiltration measurements across baseline architectures.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Empirical security validation measuring canary leakage rates across adversarial trials, audit-driven injection recovery, and task pass rates on hidden test suites.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Deterministic protocol rules and cryptographic verification checks implemented in Context Guard and SCM; no model optimization or parameter tuning was conducted.

primary.limitations: The authors clearly delineate the boundary of contextual state protection, noting that untracked workspace files rely on indirect tool ingestion, and acknowledge the deliberate fail-closed trade-off regarding system liveness during severe disruption.
primary.method_assessment: The protocol architecture and threat models are defined rigorously, supported by formal definitions, algorithms for initialization, verification, and state updates, and cryptographic correctness proofs for integrity and freshness.
primary.quality_rationale: The work provides a complete, well-reasoned systems security contribution with formal guarantees, sound implementation in DeepSeek Harness, robust experimental validation against actual attack vectors, and explicit threat boundary considerations.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper formalizes contextual state continuity and historical traceability for agentic systems, introducing ElephantAgent—a protocol combining a TEE-based Context Guard with a replicated state continuity ledger to prevent out-of-band state tampering and facilitate audit and recovery.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The work provides a complete, well-reasoned systems security contribution with formal guarantees, sound implementation in DeepSeek Harness, robust experimental validation against actual attack vectors, and explicit threat boundary considerations.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors clearly delineate the boundary of contextual state protection, noting that untracked workspace files rely on indirect tool ingestion, and acknowledge the deliberate fail-closed trade-off regarding system liveness during severe disruption.
